title: Walked to the Han River Again
description:
On the night the weight of 3 billion won pressed down, {name} closed the plan and the phone and walked all the way to the Han River for air.

Today, head full again, their feet found the same path on their own.

The river flowed on, indifferent as ever.

choices.text: Like that day — walking sorts it out
choices.result_text:
Stepping away from the numbers and moving the body.

That became {name}'s way of clearing the head.
The walk back always felt a little lighter. Today too.

choices.text: Watch the river, steady the heart again
choices.result_text:
The river reaches the sea without rushing.

{name} leaned on the railing and watched it a long while.

title: A Strange Longing
description:
The first night in the new place after escaping the goshiwon, {name} strangely missed that tiny room.

Even in somewhere wider and cleaner, it happened sometimes.

Tonight, too, that room's ceiling came back to mind.

choices.text: What I miss isn't the room — it's who I was then
choices.result_text:
What was missed wasn't the narrow room, but the self who had nothing yet dreamed big.

{name} asked whether that heart was still intact.
The room wasn't the only thing that should have grown.

choices.text: No going back now — eyes forward
choices.result_text:
Let the longing stay a longing.

That room was a station passed, not a destination.

title: A Number Kept to Myself
description:
The day {name} first crossed 100 million won, they decided to keep it to themselves and tell no one.

Good things were mostly known alone after that.

Today, looking at the account again, they briefly pictured someone to tell.

choices.text: Knowing alone is comfortable — it's my way
choices.result_text:
Achievement without announcement.

Since others' recognition wasn't the point, knowing it alone was enough.
{name} quietly closed the account. A private satisfaction lived there.

choices.text: This time, I want to share it with someone
choices.result_text:
Keeping it private is fine, but joy gets lighter when shared.

{name} looked at the contacts list for a while.

title: Saying Just a Little
description:
The day {name} told Daeun only 'investing's been going okay lately' — and stopped there.

Today Daeun asked, lightly.

'You mentioned investing back then. How's it going now? ...Never mind, you don't have to say if you don't want to.'

choices.text: Be a little more honest this time
choices.result_text:
You showed her the positions in red, not only the ones in profit.

Daeun studied the screen and said, 'Thank you for telling me. I like being able to see a little more of your world.'
After she handed the phone back, the red figures looked sharper than before.

choices.text: Draw a line and say you do not want to talk about it yet
choices.result_text:
'It's okay. You can tell me when you're ready. I won't press.'

Daeun meant it. From then on, she stopped bringing up investments first. It was easier, and a new unasked space appeared between you.

title: Showing Them the Room
description:
The day {name}'s parents came to Seoul, {name} showed them the tiny room as it was. Nothing to hide.

Today Dad brought up that day.

'That room of yours — small, but clean. That's what hurt you more, actually.'

choices.text: "I wasn't ashamed. That's where I started."
choices.result_text:
Dad was quiet for a long time.

'...Right. Nothing to be ashamed of.'

The choice not to hide that narrow room had shown his parents who their son really was.

choices.text: "I've moved somewhere better now. Come see it."
choices.result_text:
'Yeah? ...you'll have to go see it.'

A faint pride mixed into Dad's voice.

title: Not Showing Them the Room
description:
The day {name}'s parents came up, {name} only bought them a meal at a place nearby and didn't show them the room.

Today Mom mentioned it quietly.

'Minjun-ah, I wanted to see your room back then. I knew everything but pretended not to.'

choices.text: "I couldn't show it then... I'm sorry."
choices.result_text:
'Nothing to be sorry for. I understood.'

What {name} wanted to hide wasn't the room, but a self who'd achieved nothing yet.
{name} could admit that now.

choices.text: "I can show you now. I've moved somewhere better."
choices.result_text:
'...Yeah. You'd like to see it.'

In place of the room never shown, there was now a space to be proud of.

title: The Birthday I Rested
description:
On {name}'s 35th birthday, they closed the plan for that one day and just spent it as a birthday.

They think of that day sometimes.

Resting didn't break anything. If anything, the next day was lighter.

choices.text: That choice was right — rest is a strategy too
choices.result_text:
Run without stopping and something eventually snaps.

{name} knows that one day of birthday rest was maintenance the five-year run required.
Sometimes you go farther by stopping.

choices.text: I know now I need to rest more often
choices.result_text:
That day was recovery, not guilt.

{name} decided not to push so hard.

title: The Birthday I Worked
description:
On {name}'s 35th birthday, they replied briefly to the messages and pulled the plan back out.

The day they didn't stop, even on a birthday.

It came to mind today. Did you have to go that far — or is that why you're here?

choices.text: That's why I'm here — no regrets
choices.result_text:
The days you went one step further while others rested.

That accumulated into the current gap.
{name} quietly thanked the self of that birthday.

choices.text: Next birthday, a day off is allowed
choices.result_text:
That day's desperation was necessary. But not every time.

{name} knows now that living a little differently is allowed.

title: Reaching Out First
description:
At 35, in that piercingly lonely stretch, {name} reached out first to anyone at all.

That courage comes to mind sometimes.

Today, on another similarly hollow day, they picked up the phone.

choices.text: Like that time — extend a hand first
choices.result_text:
Loneliness deepens if you sit still.

That small courage to reach out first saved {name} more than once.
Today too, they checked in on someone. When a reply came, the room felt less cold.

choices.text: This time alone is fine — I've grown sturdier
choices.result_text:
Back then, anyone would do. Now, alone is bearable.

The strength to endure loneliness had grown a little.

title: Walking Alone
description:
At 35, in that lonely stretch, {name} didn't call anyone and walked alone to the Han River.

They learned to walk alone then.

Today, mood sinking again, they stood at the same riverside.

choices.text: Time walking alone fills me too
choices.result_text:
Being alone isn't always loneliness.

Time spent walking with oneself made {name} clearer.
In the river wind, they quietly made peace with today's self.

choices.text: Now I think of someone to walk with
choices.result_text:
Grown used to walking alone, but sometimes wished someone were beside them.

Watching the river, {name} briefly pictured who they'd walk this path with once it was over.

title: Going to the Hospital
description:
At 36, when the body sent signals, {name} put work aside and went to the hospital. Had to know.

They think it was the right call.

Today the body is heavy again. This is the final stretch.

choices.text: Like that time — body first
choices.result_text:
Collapsing right at the finish line means nothing.

As going to the hospital protected {name} then, they chose the body first today too.
No health, no Gangnam.

choices.text: Trust the test results — pace it, no overreach
choices.result_text:
Thanks to that checkup, {name} knows their own condition.

Instead of running blindly, they found a sustainable speed.

title: Putting the Body Off
description:
At 36, when the body sent signals, {name} brushed it off — 'can't stop now, you'll rest later.'

That 'later' is now.

The body is signaling again, louder this time.

choices.text: Not putting it off this time — go to the hospital
choices.result_text:
The price of putting it off came back as a bigger signal.

This time {name} didn't delay.
Learned the body is like debt — put it off and the interest compounds.

choices.text: Just a little more — rest properly when it's over
choices.result_text:
Put it off again. Because the finish line is in sight.

But it was 'just a little more' that time too.

title: For Asking
description:
While Hyun-su was drifting, {name} didn't just pass by — they asked, 'What are you up to these days?'

Today Hyun-su reached out.

'Hyung, I was really at rock bottom then. You asking — it made me feel like someone was watching out for me.'

choices.text: "It was nothing. You held on well."
choices.result_text:
'It was all thanks to you, really.'

A nothing word becomes a rope for someone.
{name} was glad they hadn't just walked past that time.

choices.text: "I wished someone would've asked me back then too."
choices.result_text:
'...So you went through that too, hyung.'

There are people who give what they never received.

title: Cutting SNS Off
description:
In the second year in Seoul, shaken by news of friends doing well, {name} decided: 'Cut SNS. Comparison is poison for focus.'

They hadn't looked at the feed since.

Today they happened to hear someone's update — the kind of news that once would have rattled them.

choices.text: No longer shaken — I have my own pace
choices.result_text:
Not watching others' speed, they could see their own.

{name} knows now that cutting SNS was a choice for focus, not escape.
From a place free of comparison, their own path was clearer.

choices.text: Sometimes I'm curious — but I still don't look
choices.result_text:
There was curiosity. But {name} knows its cost too.

After a brief hesitation, they set the phone down.
